translations.answer: The old implementation treated torch.isclose(computed_torque, applied_torque) as a flag for overflow, which is the opposite: equality indicates no clipping, and inequality indicates clipping. PR #3163 has been merged and replaced with ~torch.isclose, with regression tests covering 0/0 and 100/50 scenarios on CPU/CUDA and 1/2 Panda articulation. This detector only identifies differences between computed and applied torque and cannot replace real actuator limits or hardware safety protection.
translations.applicability: Applies to versions using Isaac Lab joint_effort_out_of_limit to compare computed/applied torque; original post environment was the Isaac Sim 5.0 feature branch.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict, and there is formal documentation or precise independent replication.
translations.details.attempts.0: Original post provided a single joint minimum reproduction and two assertions.
translations.details.attempts.1: PR #3163 reverses the isclose result and adds two regression test cases for CPU/CUDA and 1/2 Panda articulation.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: A truth table for no clipping and clipping is used to test the termination predicate, not just from the function name.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Prints computed_torque, applied_torque, and the termination boolean to confirm whether the inequality is from actuator clipping.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use the merged PR #3163: out_of_limits = ~torch.isclose(computed_torque, applied_torque), and apply any to the joint dimension.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab commit b5d094e5de0d35d0f6f87a0709394cbe230159d9 (feature/isaacsim_5_0); Isaac Sim 5.0; Ubuntu 22.04; RTX 5080; CUDA 12.8; GPU driver 570.144.
translations.details.environments.1: PR #3163 regression test parameterized coverage of CPU and cuda:0,1,2 with 2 Panda articulation.
translations.details.limits.0: The function evaluates whether computed and applied torque are different due to clipping, and does not validate the effort limit against real motor, reducer, and thermal limits.
translations.details.limits.1: Comparison still uses the default tolerance of torch.isclose; small differences are classified based on this tolerance.
translations.details.limits.2: PR test passes by directly filling computed/applied buffer to simulate clipping, not real motor or physical actuator clipping experiments.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR #3163 merged on 2025-08-21, merged commit a60168a2dc0b7f56f76b8985d0bca2e79a4e5ef6; 0.45.3 changelog explicitly records the fix for reversed effort-limit report.
translations.details.outcomes.1: Regression test confirms 0/0 does not terminate, 100/50 does terminate.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does joint_effort_out_of_limit terminate when torque is not clipped, but not when it is clipped?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Real-world WBC should not treat this software predicate as the sole torque safety chain; hardware limit flow, thermal protection, and independent emergency stop are still required.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Old implementation directly used torch.isclose result as out_of_limits, but the function definition states equality exactly indicates no clipping.
translations.details.symptoms.0: When computed_torque == applied_torque == 0, the predicate should not terminate, but the old logic returns True.
translations.details.symptoms.1: When computed_torque=100 and applied_torque=50, the predicate should terminate, but the old logic returns False.
translations.source.locator: Isaac Lab #3155 truth table reproduction; author's reply to issuecomment-3179329133; merged PR #3163, regression test, and 0.45.3 changelog.
translations.source.title: Isaac Lab joint_effort_out_of_limit termination condition and truth value flipped.
translations.title: Why does Isaac Lab's joint_effort_out_of_limit terminate when torque is not clipped, but not when it is clipped?
